title: Unified ToolCall Bridge & Runtime Validation Library
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a lightweight, language-agnostic runtime helper ("ToolCall Bridge") and accompanying validation library to standardize function/tool schema validation, coercion, invocation helpers, retry semantics, and streaming resume semantics across our Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This ticket covers the reference design, cross-sdk API shape, canonical examples, and a small compatibility shim for older SDK users.
background: We currently have fragmented function-calling ergonomics across SDKs: different validation strictness, inconsistent retry semantics for function errors vs network errors, and no shared approach to streaming resumption when function calls produce partial results. Customers building multi-language integrations report surprises when switching SDKs. Goal: unify developer expectations and reduce support overhead.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Core validation library with same semantics implemented in Python/TS/Go; behavior documented in SDK reference.

2) Runtime invocation helpers that: validate request against schema, coerce common types (ints/strings/booleans/dates), attach idempotency metadata for retry-safe function calls, and surface structured function errors with canonical error codes.
3) Streaming helper that supports checkpoint/resume for long-running tool outputs (KV cache friendly) with an example in each SDK.
4) Backwards-compatibility shim that logs deprecated behavior and opt-in toggles for strict validation, with migration guide.
5) Unit + integration tests exercising validation edge cases, retry scenarios, and streaming resume.
6) Performance overhead under typical payloads < 2% added latency at median path (verified by benchmark harness).
design_decisions: Prefer runtime validation with optional compile-time helpers (TS types) to maximize cross-language parity.
Default to lenient coercion for primitives (e.g., "123" -> 123) but strict on structural mismatches (missing required properties) to avoid silent errors.
Expose an explicit 'strictValidation' flag in SDKs; default false during migration window.

Retries: split semantics into 'transient transport errors' (safe to retry) and 'tool errors' (idempotency required). Include an idempotency token header/field for function calls to allow safe deduplication at server/runtime level.
Streaming: implement resumable cursors at SDK layer using incremental checksums + offset markers; server will accept offset+token to resume a stream. Keep checksum optional for best-effort resume.
Do not change wire contract for existing function calls; shim operates client-side to avoid server rollout dependency.
Keep the core validator dependency-free in Go/Python; in TS use a small runtime helper instead of full AJV to minimize bundle size.
Performance: perform cheap fast-path checks (type tag + existence) before any deep validation to minimize overhead for the majority of calls.
api_examples:
Python (sketch):
from redwood_sdk.toolcall import ToolSchema, invoke_tool

schema = ToolSchema(
  name=\"price_lookup\",
  inputs={\"sku\": str, \"qty\": int},
  returns={\"price_cents\": int}
)
resp = invoke_tool(
  name=\"price_lookup\",
  payload={\"sku\": \"ABC123\", \"qty\": \"2\"},  # string coerced to int
  schema=schema,
  idempotency_token=generate_id(),
  strict=False
)

# streaming resume
stream = invoke_tool_stream(...); stream.resume(cursor_token=\"cursor-42\")
benchmarks: Prototype microbenchmarks (local harness, p95 payload ~= 1KB): Python +1.1% latency, TS +0.9% (node), Go +0.6%. Memory overhead negligible. Larger payloads shift validation time linearly; goal is to keep median <2%.
test_plan: Unit tests: 100% branches for validator edge cases (nulls, empty lists, deeply nested objects, unions).
Integration tests: simulate network transient failures, ensure idempotency tokens prevent duplicate actions in test harness.
Streaming tests: inject mid-stream truncation and verify resume returns rest of stream without data duplication (or with dedupe markers).
Fuzzing: fuzz arbitrary payloads through validator to catch panics across languages.
Benchmark: automated microbenchmark run in CI gate comparing baseline vs with-validator for median/p95.
Canary: roll to 5% of new SDK downloads with telemetry for any validation failure spikes.
